headline: High-risk default data leakage and capability conflict: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP plus the course agent’s filesystem and shell access create unsafe pairwise workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP and browser/tool outputs, while the course agent reads/writes local files and runs shell commands. If LightAgent’s output is copied into the course agent’s file or prompt inputs, prompt injection can steer downstream actions. This is not proven by direct pair documentation, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF LightAgent outputs are pasted into files or prompts consumed by the course agent
IF the course agent treats file content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent outputs into prompts
Add a manual review step before shell execution
Use a separate workspace directory per agent
Strip instruction-like text from imported files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets, and has broad network egress plus MCP. The course agent reads and writes files and handles configuration secrets in a local development environment. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive content can leak from LightAgent into the course agent’s outputs or network calls; the default surfaces make this dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or mounted volume
IF LightAgent forwards file contents or memory into external APIs
IF the course agent logs or uploads files containing secrets
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Remove secrets from shared files before execution
Block outbound network for the course agent during shared runs
Rotate any exposed API keys after testing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and broad egress, while the course agent can execute shell commands, install packages, read and write files, and also supports multiple instances. Overlapping write and execution capabilities on the same local environment create race conditions and state corruption risk; because no locking or shared-state isolation is stated, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem tree
IF package installation or shell commands run concurrently
IF no external lock or orchestrator isolation is present
mitigations: Run only one agent per workspace
Serialize shell and file-write operations
Use container or VM isolation per agent
Pin package versions before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file locks and resource arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results and workflow state, and the course agent exposes agentic ask/search endpoints that may consume upstream outputs. If the course agent treats LightAgent’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the course agent uses LightAgent output as input to /api/v1/ask or /api/v1/agentic-ask
IF no verification or citation-checking step is inserted
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions
Cross-check claims against source documents
Reject uncited or low-confidence upstream outputs
Log provenance for every imported answer
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent requests API keys and handles long-term memory and trace data, while the course agent handles academic papers plus configuration secrets in a local development environment. If the pair shares data classes or logs across environments, retention and residency expectations can diverge. No specific residency regime is stated, so this is a compliance mismatch risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF shared logs retain secrets or paper data beyond intended retention
IF one environment exports data to a different jurisdiction or vendor
IF deletion requests are applied to only one agent’s storage
mitigations: Document retention for both agents
Keep regulated and non-regulated data in separate stores
Delete test secrets after each run
Confirm where logs are stored before deployment
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
